title: Level 3 Comprehensive Assessment
slides.0.title: 📋 Level 3 Comprehensive Assessment
slides.1.title: 🎯 Level 3 Key Takeaways
slides.1.points.0: 🍇 Northern Italian rare varieties: Timorasso (Piemonte), Ruché, Erbaluce, Nosiola (Trentino)
slides.1.points.1: 🍊 The orange wine revolution: Josko Gravner revived ancient skin-contact amphorae fermentation in Friuli
slides.1.points.2: 🗺️ MGA system: Barolo/Barbaresco single-vineyard classification (Menzione Geografica Aggiuntiva)
slides.1.points.3: 🔍 Label reading: the government numbered seal (fascetta) is the hardest-to-fake DOCG identifier
slides.1.points.4: 👑 Sassicaia: the only Italian DOC named after a single estate (Bolgheri Sassicaia)
slides.1.points.5: 📅 Vintage assessment: harvest-season climate is the decisive factor — late-ripening varieties are most affected by late summer and autumn rain
slides.1.points.6: 🏠 Ideal cellar conditions: 12–14°C, 70–75% humidity, avoid dramatic temperature fluctuations
slides.1.points.7: 👁️ SAT blind tasting: Sight → Aroma → Taste
slides.1.points.8: 🎯 Variety identification: Nebbiolo's fingerprint = 'tar + roses + dried leaves' + orange rim
slides.1.points.9: 🏭 Cooperative model accounts for over 50% of Italy's total wine production — significant economies of scale
slides.1.points.10: 🌍 The United States is Italy's largest wine export market by value
slides.1.points.11: 🌿 Biodynamic Preparation 500: fermented cow manure in cow horn, then sprayed to activate soil life
slides.1.points.12: 🌡️ Climate warming: higher-altitude northern Italy benefits short-term (better ripeness); long-term risks remain
slides.1.points.13: 🍽️ BTG strategy: choose wines with good post-opening stability that pair across multiple courses
